newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Mar household spending up due to tax - agency.
newsitem.headline: Japan Mar household spending up due to tax - agency.

text.p: A rise in household spending in Japan in March was mainly due to a rush of buying prior to the consumption tax increase on April 1, an official from the Management and Coordination Agency told reporters on Tuesday.
The tax was raised to five percent from three percent.
Japan's household spending in March rose 5.8 percent year-on-year in real terms to an average 374,061 yen per household, the agency reported earlier on Tuesday.

"Household spending as a trend is continuing its gradual recovery. We have to see how much spending will fall in April and May to determine the extent of the impact (of the tax increase) on the data," the official said.
The 5.8 percent increase in overall household spending in March was the biggest since February 1992, when it grew 6.4 percent, the official said.
The growth in spending in February 1992, however, was due to the effect of a leap year, he said.
"Excluding the leap year factor, the rise was the biggest since the consumption tax was first introduced (in April 1989)," he said.
Overall household spending grew a real 6.3 percent in March 1989, the month before the tax was introduced.
